cells.tense: The understanding has landed and the person is standing in it, pen in hand.
cells.ask: Name the pattern you have already found in one situation, then take one step that follows from it — today, before it goes fuzzy.
cells.core:
You've looked at one thing long enough that nothing in it is hiding from you. You know how the parts connect, why it went the way it did, where it was heading. And the pull toward what you actually want isn't a fantasy in your head — it points at the same thing your understanding points at.

What this balance is free to feed next is thinking that comes after understanding, not more looking. Pattern recognition that loosens something instead of replacing it with a tidy answer. You already have the shape. The next move is to act from it, or hand it to somebody who needs it — either way it stops being yours alone. That's what the completion is for.
cells.sheetLine: You saw it through. Now act like you did.
cells.verb: seeing all the way through what was in front of you
cells.place: the direction you steer by and the light it keeps naming

cells.tense: You are trying to finish understanding what has not arrived yet, bracing for a conclusion ahead of the evidence.
cells.ask: Pick one thing you keep trying to finish understanding and leave it open for a day. Come back tomorrow with no conclusion ready.
cells.core:
You want the full picture before you move, and so you keep examining past where the examining can go. Some of the material isn't here yet — the other person hasn't spoken, the result isn't in — and you're already writing the ending. The completion you're producing is real, it's just early.

The end you keep reaching stops being the end of anything you actually saw. The direction stops guiding and becomes a demand. What's underneath is the pull toward light turned into a test: prove you can see it all, prove the light is really there. The light doesn't need the proof. It's already what you go by.
cells.sheetLine: You are finishing a picture the evidence hasn't finished.
cells.verb: seeing all the way through what was in front of you
cells.place: the direction you steer by and the light it keeps naming

cells.tense: The understanding happened once and you have not stood in it since, still at a door already behind you.
cells.ask: Write down one thing you already understand, plainly, in your own hand. Then choose a small direction from it before the day ends.
cells.core:
You've done the work. The understanding is still in you — the shape of how it works, why it went the way it did. But the pull toward what you want has gone quiet, and the direction is hard to make out from where you're standing. So what you know sits there unused while you stay parked.

This isn't a missing insight. It's a choice that hasn't been made. The seed of directed form starts as one decision held in your hand, not invested yet, only picked up. Pick up one small one and the pull toward what you want starts moving again — not because you feel inspired, but because you're acting from what you know.
cells.sheetLine: You already see it. You're just not choosing from it.
cells.verb: seeing all the way through what was in front of you
cells.place: the direction you steer by and the light it keeps naming

cells.tense: You are already moving by a direction you keep describing as something you haven't settled on.
cells.ask: Say out loud one thing you have been calling undecided. Then let the next small move follow from it.
cells.core:
The orientation is running. It shows in what you pay attention to, what you say yes to, the things you keep coming back to — while you talk about the whole question as still open. A direction is doing its work on you now.

What hasn't happened is the claim. It's easier to call the picture unfinished than to say what it already points at. But you are the turning point, not a person waiting to find one. What's arriving now is recognition, not discovery. The next moment doesn't need the whole map. It needs the direction you keep using said out loud once.
cells.sheetLine: You're already moving by a light you say you haven't settled.

attempts.check: Clarity is rendered as a bound capacity whose completion is full seeing; the claim to watch is that this person has finished seeing. A reader could rightly answer that something new is still coming into view. If that is so, the ask still stands: a viewing that takes ten minutes is useful even if the investigation is not over. The line that serves me more than the person is 'nothing left to see,' so the cells narrow it to the viewing already done on one subject.
